_why: Chat's rules as cases, one table for two readers (CLAUDE.md rules 1 and 3). waWindow, contactChannel and contactTemplateText live in nala-shared.js for the page and again in worker/guest-contact.js, because a Worker cannot import from the site: the page previews what the Worker sends and says when the 24 hours close, and the Worker refuses free text outside them. contact_suite.py runs the page's copies through this table and worker/contact-test.mjs the Worker's; a case added here fails whichever copy has not learned it. contactRowState is the page's alone, pinned here all the same because it is the colour a row wears, and so are contactTeams and teamsOf, the team list every page offers (29 Sep).

window._note: [guest's last WhatsApp message, now, open?, closes at]. Meta's rule: free text only within 24 hours of the guest's last WhatsApp message. Stamps are compared as instants, whatever zone they were written in.

channel._note: [thread, now, which way a message from us goes]. none: texted STOP. wa: WhatsApp free text. watpl: WhatsApp, approved wording only. sms: SMS free text. A guest who wrote in the last 24 hours is answered the way they wrote; otherwise WhatsApp only for a guest who agreed (the desk's switch, or they once wrote there) and whose number WhatsApp knows.

row._note: [thread, unsorted messages, open tasks, has a sendable mobile, the row's state]. fresh is white (work to do), task amber, sent the waiting grey, done white too (the owner, 30 Sep: green would be nearly every card), none and nophone sunk.

templates._note: [template, first name, arrival day, the words]. The approved WhatsApp wording, as the preview shows it and the Worker records it. GUEST-CONTACT.md holds the same text with {{1}} and {{2}} for Meta.
cases: Hi James, it's Nala Resort with a quick question about your stay. Could you reply to this message when you have a moment?
Hi there, it's Nala Resort with a quick question about your stay. Could you reply to this message when you have a moment?
Hi Léa, it's Nala Resort with a quick question about your stay. Could you reply to this message when you have a moment?
Hi James, we look forward to welcoming you to Nala Resort on Saturday 3 October. If there is anything we can prepare before you arrive, just reply to this message.
Hi James, we look forward to welcoming you to Nala Resort on Saturday 3 October. If there is anything we can prepare before you arrive, just reply to this message.
Hi there, we look forward to welcoming you to Nala Resort on your arrival day. If there is anything we can prepare before you arrive, just reply to this message.

teams._note: [/contactsettings, all?, the list as [key, label, retired?]]. contactTeams, the one reading of the team list (29 Sep, editable in Settings > General, Teams): the six the owner started with, under whatever name Settings gave them, then each team added there, oldest first. A removed team is retired, never deleted: without all it is gone from the list, with all it is there, marked, so its tasks keep its name. A node that is not a team - a bad key, no name and not one of the six, not an object - is no team.

grants._note: [role, /permissions, editBookings, guestReply]. Who may use the desk and who may reply to a guest, as can() answers it on the page and mayDo in worker/guest-contact.js, which refuses what the page would not offer. guestReply (30 Sep, the owner: a switch in Settings for a role being able to respond to messages): shipped on for the admin, the manager and the waiter; the Roles switches move it for the chef, the waiter and housekeeping. The admin and the manager are never switched off, and the rules refuse the matrix a column for either, the masseuse or a machine. A value that is not true or false is no opinion.

teamsof._note: [/contactsettings, a login's email, the teams whose tasks it sees]. teamsOf: the teams a login is switched on for in Settings, in the list's order; a retired team is nobody's. The email is keyed as emailKey keys it.
